tasks.short: Prepare and submit insurance applications and related business or government forms.

steps.what: Read application documents and identify required fields.

loop.input: Application documents and a fixed field schema.
loop.output: Draft application fields with source locations and uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Validate types, required fields and cross-document consistency. Preserve source evidence.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document. Send unresolved fields to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured forms need only mapping. Remaining attachments contain variable free text.

steps.what: Check application fields against insurance policy administration records in {OTHER}.
Ask the policyholder or representative for missing information and clarify conflicting answers.
Populate the required form and assemble its supporting evidence.
Check declarations, submit through the appropriate portal, and retain the acknowledgement.

tasks.design: A records view in the {OTHER} insurance policy administration system checks required fields and exposes missing information. A bounded reader handles residual documents in the {DOCS}; a generator assembles the submission package. After an authorised signatory approves declarations, a connector submits through the {PARTNER_PORTAL} or {GOV_PORTAL} and stores the acknowledgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Variable attachments, changing form versions and disconnected portals made mapping and maintenance expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing validation and template features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can shorten connector development; bounded extraction handles residual free text.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous declarations, unavailable portal interfaces and responsibility for legally significant submissions remain. GDPR applies, including controls for special-category data.
tasks.human_edge: Clarify what an applicant means and recognise when a declaration needs an underwriter or authorised signatory.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time resolving ambiguous applications and helping applicants prepare complete evidence. They gain delegated control over completeness checks, with coverage and declaration authority staying with authorised roles.

reach.task: Analyse recurring causes of application rework.
reach.learn: Process mapping, exception sampling and form-version analysis.

evidence.claim: Insurance correspondence and attachments can be organised into case files.
Field validation, template generation and approved submission can use deterministic software.
Document extraction evidence supports intake feasibility, not automatic underwriting or filing accuracy.

assumptions: The baseline is carrier applications; government forms arise only where required.
Missing-information contact is conditional; its time share is averaged across cases.
Structured inputs bypass document extraction.
Estimates cover one form family and one submission route with existing access.
Consultation under national rules is assessed during rollout; new employee monitoring is outside scope.
unknowns: Which forms, insurance lines and languages dominate the workload?
Which submission routes offer supported interfaces?
Who may approve declarations and submit each form?
What data access, retention and national consultation requirements apply locally?
research_questions: Which required fields can come directly from existing records?
Can submission acknowledgements be retrieved and matched without duplicate filings?
Which declaration errors cause the most costly rework?
new_work: Review uncertain extraction and conflicting application fields.
Maintain field mappings, form versions and submission rules.
Resolve rejected submissions and reconcile missing acknowledgements.

tasks.short: Match initial premium payments, record collection and issue receipts.

steps.what: Retrieve the initial premium due from insurance policy administration in {OTHER}.
Check cleared payments and match payment references to the premium due.
Clarify unmatched payments or disputed premium amounts with the policyholder.
Record the cleared premium against the policy and receivable.
Generate and send the initial premium receipt.

tasks.design: Configure payment matching in the {ERP} using cleared transactions from the {BANK}. A small integration updates the {OTHER} insurance policy administration system and triggers its approved receipt template through the {EMAIL}. Unmatched amounts enter a work queue for clarification.
tasks.previous_blocker: Payment references and policy identifiers did not reliably connect financial and policy records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing matching and receipt features handle the routine work. A small deterministic integration can close the remaining record gap.
tasks.still_hard: Third-party payers, combined transfers, reversals and disputed amounts need investigation. Receipt issuance must follow the correct cleared-payment event.
tasks.human_edge: Explain discrepancies and agree the next step when a policyholder disputes the amount or needs help paying.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of unresolved initial premium payments

tasks.altitude: The clerk works mainly on unmatched payments and customer explanations. They can prioritise investigation within agreed limits; refund, premium-change and coverage rights do not expand.

reach.task: Measure why initial premium payments remain unmatched.
reach.learn: Receivables reconciliation, ageing analysis and payment-reference design.

evidence.claim: Structured payment matching and receipt generation usually require rules and configuration rather than a model.
For a digital payment baseline, the steps support substantial automation despite the task's human classification.

assumptions: Most initial premiums arrive through electronic payment routes.
The task starts from an agreed premium amount.
Customer payment authorisation remains with the customer; this design does not initiate new debits.
Unresolved exceptions remain unallocated until clarified.
Estimates cover one payment feed and one policy-record interface.
GDPR and applicable national consultation rules are assessed during access and rollout.
unknowns: How often are cash, cheques or other offline payments used?
Which matching and receipt features are already configured?
What event confirms payment clearance for each route?
Who may resolve allocation exceptions or authorise refunds?
research_questions: Can unique payment references remove most matching exceptions?
How should reversals affect receipts and collection status?
Can duplicate events be replayed without duplicate postings or receipts?
new_work: Investigate unmatched payments and failed deliveries.
Reconcile collection records across financial and policy records.
Maintain matching tolerances and reversal rules.

tasks.short: Interview policyholders, answer claims questions and record information from customer calls.

steps.what: Open the claim and review policy details in insurance claims administration in {OTHER}.
Verify the caller's identity and authority to discuss the claim.
Listen to the account, ask follow-up questions and capture relevant claim facts.
Consult approved guidance and explain claim status and required next steps.

loop.input: Customer question, current claim status and approved policy guidance.
loop.output: Suggested explanation with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require current sources and matching policy version. The clerk checks before speaking.
loop.stop: One retrieval and one draft per question. Missing or conflicting evidence goes to a specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Status fields use fixed text. Varied customer questions need bounded reading of approved guidance.

steps.what: Write the call summary and update claim facts.

loop.input: Clerk-entered interview notes and agreed next steps.
loop.output: Structured call summary and proposed claim-field updates.
loop.check: Link proposed facts to notes. Preserve uncertainty and distinguish customer statements from verified facts.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction attempt. The clerk completes unresolved fields manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text accounts need summarisation; fixed fields and task creation remain deterministic.

steps.what: Assign follow-up work or refer the claim to the appropriate specialist.

tasks.design: The {OTHER} insurance claims administration system presents a prepared case view and an approved question checklist. A bounded answer desk reads the {DOCS} and current claim status, while a separate bounded drafting step turns the clerk's notes into proposed updates. The clerk controls the conversation and approves saved facts; configured routing creates follow-up work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Claim context and guidance were scattered, while callers' accounts did not fit fixed fields.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case views can gather structured context. Bounded drafting can reduce searching and paperwork without replacing the interview.
tasks.still_hard: Distress, conflicting accounts, accessibility needs and disputed coverage require skilled conversation. GDPR applies; solely automated decisions with significant effects require Article 22 assessment and applicable safeguards.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, notice uncertainty and distress, and ask a question the checklist did not anticipate.

ambition.what: Scheduled claims preparation calls for policyholders needing extra support

tasks.altitude: More of the week goes to useful conversations and difficult follow-up. With delegated authority, the clerk can arrange support calls and specialist referrals; claim settlement rights do not change.

reach.task: Plan assisted contact capacity around customer needs.
reach.learn: Accessible service design, queue planning and referral criteria.

evidence.claim: A documented regulator study found flagged insurance claims were referred to people.
Transcription can invent content, supporting source checks if audio capture is later introduced.
GDPR Article 22 governs qualifying solely automated decisions, with exceptions and safeguards.
Case preparation, note drafting and routing can change independently of the human conversation.

assumptions: The baseline uses clerk-entered notes; recording and transcription are outside scope.
The answer desk explains existing status and guidance rather than deciding coverage.
Routine identity checks remain part of the human call.
The conversation steps outweigh the prior suggesting this task vanishes.
Estimates cover one claims queue and a maintained guidance collection.
Access review includes GDPR and employee consultation under applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which callers and claim types need specialist handling?
Are approved guidance and policy versions reliably maintained?
What identity checks and disclosure permissions apply?
Can proposed field changes be staged before saving?
research_questions: Which call questions can be answered entirely from structured status fields?
How often do draft summaries omit uncertainty or misattribute a statement?
Does reduced paperwork improve resolution without rushing callers?
new_work: Review suggested explanations and proposed claim updates.
Maintain approved guidance and routing rules.
Sample summaries for unsupported facts and lost uncertainty.
Handle unanswered questions and arrange specialist support.

tasks.short: Retrieve policy cancellation lists for servicing work.

steps.what: Retrieve the cancellation list from insurance policy administration in {OTHER}.
Print the cancellation list and place it with the servicing papers.

tasks.design: Configure a scheduled, access-controlled cancellation view in the {OTHER} insurance policy administration system. Servicing staff open the current view directly, removing the routine printout.
tasks.previous_blocker: An inherited paper handoff and unconfigured report scheduling kept retrieval manual.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved filters and scheduled views are established capabilities. No model or new technical breakthrough is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Correct effective dates, rescinded cancellations and stale source records can make a list misleading. Physical archives need separate digitisation if they remain material.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an incorrect policy match or misleading cancellation status before downstream servicing action.
tasks.altitude: Routine retrieval and printing disappear from the week. Decision rights do not change; this task retrieves records and does not authorise cancellations.

reach.task: Retrieve other recurring servicing exception lists.
reach.learn: Record filters, effective-date logic and access permissions.

evidence.claim: Scheduled record views can replace manual retrieval and routine printing without a model.
Retrieving a cancellation list is separate from deciding or executing a policy cancellation.

assumptions: Electronic cancellation records are the typical baseline; physical cards are a legacy exception.
The printout has no independent legal or operational requirement.
An existing report or saved-view feature is available.
Estimates exclude bulk scanning of physical archives.
GDPR access and retention controls apply. Consultation under national rules is assessed if working practices change materially.
unknowns: Are cancellation records electronic, physical or mixed?
Why is the list currently printed?
Which dates and statuses define the correct cancellation population?
Can the existing view refresh automatically with suitable permissions?
research_questions: Can the existing scheduled report remove the retrieval step immediately?
How are reinstatements and rescinded cancellations reflected?
Can staff see source freshness and record counts?
new_work: Maintain selection criteria and access permissions.
Investigate missing, stale or unexpected records.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward resolving incomplete applications, payment discrepancies and difficult customer accounts. Staff can gain delegated control over completeness checks and referral priorities; underwriting, cancellation and settlement authority remain explicitly assigned.
reach: Management analyst: investigate recurring rework and payment exceptions.
Administrative services manager: plan assisted customer contact and queue capacity.
Office clerk: extend reliable record retrieval to adjacent servicing work.
skills_to_grow: Read validation results and investigate exceptions.
Check extracted facts against source evidence.
Understand payment reconciliation and effective dates.
Maintain templates, routing rules and approved guidance.
role.ambitious_version: Offer an assisted application and claims preparation service that helps policyholders assemble complete evidence, understand next steps and reach the right authorised specialist.

job.title: Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks
